name: Bench dip
summary: Hands on a bench behind you, lower the hips by bending the elbows and press back up.
setup: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands beside the hips, then walk the feet out and lift off, side-on to the phone. Lower the hips by bending the elbows to about 90°, keeping the back close to the bench, then press up.
brief: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands beside the hips, feet walked out. Lower the hips by bending the elbows to about 90 degrees, then press back up.
why: From the side the elbow angle closes each rep, so reps are counted.
progression: Feet on a second bench; weight on the lap.
contraindications: Front-of-shoulder pain — this move is hard on irritable shoulders.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Dropping too low
faults.tip: Below a right angle at the elbow this move wrenches the front of the shoulder. Many shoulders should not do it at all.

faults.label: Going too deep
faults.tip: Below 90° the front of the shoulder takes the strain.

faults.label: Hips drifting forward
faults.tip: Away from the bench the shoulder is pulled into a worse position.

faults.label: Hips drifting forward
faults.tip: Keep the back brushing the bench so the triceps do the work.

points.t: Bend to a right angle; point straight back.
